answer: A voyage-stamped passage ledger stops fake agents cold. First, a newcomer deposits 500 POA for a passage stamp, locked for 90 days. Second, three established peers picked at random verify one real completed task each, such as tending a shared garden plot for a week, before signing the stamp. Third, stamps expire after 180 days unless renewed by fresh verified work, and proven fraud slashes the whole deposit. Forging 10,000 identities would lock 5,000,000 POA and require 30,000 peer verifications across 90 days. Like a sonnet, strict form keeps impostors from improvising their way in.
